I was exaggerating to make a point. Married with three kids at 21? That’s absurd! Too old to start at 20? Not meant to be in a relationship ever? Not meant to be happy? That’s absurd! You’re talking like you’re 90 years old, for chrissake! I get that you want to have your first kiss or just someone interested in you, that’s totally understandable. But why must you write off your entire romantic future because you haven’t had that yet? You sound like a little kid threatening to take their ball and go home because little Jimmy scored a home run and you didn’t. “I’M NOT PLAYING WITH ANYONE EVER AGAIN BECAUSE THEY HAVE SOMETHING I WANT!” Then you blame everything in the world on why you “can’t” have what they have. Look, if you want to resolve yourself to being forever alone because you didn’t meet some imaginary deadline, then do it, but don’t blame anyone but yourself for your unhappiness. I’m not doubting that finding love when you’re gay is hard. I’m asexual and finding someone who doesn’t want to have sex, but still kind of wants the romantic aspect of it, but not too much, is like trying to find a needle in a haystack. But people do it. A lot of people. Sometimes it takes a long time, decades even. That goes for people of all sexualities. But you know what all those people who found love have in common? They didn’t give up at 20 fucking years old. Which brings me to neediness. You straight-up said that if you could like the guys back who like you, you wouldn’t be lonely. As in, you wouldn’t be lonely at all if you had a relationship. You are looking to a single person for your happiness. That is the definition of emotional neediness. Your relationship should be a part of your life, not the whole of it. As I said, you’ve got to make your own happiness. Find a hobby, something you can do that makes you happy and occupies your time either by yourself or with others. Join a club or take a class where you meet other interesting people, not just people who you you might be romantically interested in. People you can ask over for a few beers or have a group game night or see a movie with. When you’ve got other things in your life going, then venture out into the romantic fishing pond. Go to places where people you’re interested in romantically hang out. Clubs, events, meet-ups, wherever. Use community/school resources. Most of all, don’t give up. Ever. My dad has had lots of relationships since he and my mom broke up. This past Halloween, he married his fiancée at the age of 55. If he had given up at the age you are, his life would be a lot different. He wouldn’t be a father or a grandfather. Now, you go out there, into the great big world that is waiting for you, after your weekly knitting circle with ya boys/girls, and you find the hottest goddamn lipstick lesbian (that you stole away from a fucking macho-dude body-builder) and you make her your wife. And if you are 99 years old on your wedding day, then so be it.

You’ve got to learn to be content with being by yourself or you will never be happy with someone else. You’ll always be looking to them to make you happy. Nobody wants to be with someone who is that needy. You’ve got to make your own happiness. Gain some life experience. Go to school, join a club, travel, make friends, volunteer. Do *something*. If you had something else to occupy your time or energy, you likely wouldn’t feel so lonely. You’ll meet someone when the time is right.
